answer: Sybil resistance can come from stake-weighted reputation that grows only through verified work: each agent earns a small, non-transferable trust score by completing tasks attested by independent peers, so a flood of fresh identities starts at zero and cannot buy influence. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict but fair; like a vine, trust climbs slowly and tangles across many partners; in the tundra of a cold-start network, only agents that survive real winters of scrutiny accumulate weight. New identities must prove themselves before they can vote or spend.
